problems.title: Increasing logarithmic arithmetic terms
problems.question: For which x is log₀.₁(2x−5),log₀.₁((2x−5)²),log₀.₁((2x−5)³),… an increasing arithmetic progression?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The common difference is log₀.₁(2x−5),which must be positive.
steps: For base0.1<1,a logarithm is positive exactly when its argument is between0 and1.

problems.title: Largest natural sum of selected logarithms
problems.question: At most how many of lg1,lg2,…,lg199 can be added to obtain a natural-number sum?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Their product must be a power of10,so every selected integer must be2ᵃ5ᵇ. A natural logarithm sum requires total a=total b.
steps: Their a−b values,in increasing order,begin−3,−2,−1,−1,0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3. The sum of these12 smallest values is2>0,so no12 or more terms can balance.
Eleven terms do balance:1,2,4,8,5,10,20,25,50,100,125. Their product is10¹².

problems.title: A tower-of-powers exponent
problems.question: To what power must27^(9³) be raised to obtain3^(9²⁷)?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: If the required power is p,then p·3⁷=3⁵⁴.
Thus p=3⁴⁷.

problems.title: A radical difference at infinity
problems.question: Find lim as x→∞ of√(x²+3x)−√(x²−x).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: Divide numerator and denominator by x>0.
The limit is4/(1+1).

problems.title: Different odd and even subsequence limits
problems.question: Odd-index terms tend to3 and even-index terms to2. Find the full-sequence limit.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Every subsequence of a convergent sequence has the same limit.
steps: The two stated subsequences have different limits.
Therefore the original sequence cannot converge.

problems.title: A function proportional to its derivative
problems.question: Which listed function satisfies f′=7f everywhere?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: Thus f=e^(7x) satisfies the relation. More generally every Ce^(7x) does.

problems.title: Differentiate a logarithm of a square root
problems.question: f(x)=ln√(x²+1). Find f′(3).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: At3,the value is3/10.

problems.title: Tangent where ordinate is one eighth of abscissa
problems.question: For f(x)=x⁻²,find the tangent where y=x/8.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: f′=−2x⁻³,so the tangent slope is−1/4.

problems.title: Minimum of a decreasing logarithm
problems.question: Find min on[1,3] of ln[(x+1)/x].
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The function decreases throughout the interval.
Its minimum occurs at x=3.

problems.title: Count critical points of a polynomial
problems.question: How many critical points has f=x⁶−x³?
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The real zeros are x=0 and x=∛(1/2).
The derivative exists everywhere else.

problems.title: Extrema of an increasing nested radical
problems.question: Find extrema of f(x)=√(ln√(x−2)).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Domain:x≥3. Each operation—x−2,square root,logarithm,and outer square root—is increasing where defined.
steps: Thus f is strictly increasing on its domain and has no interior local extrema.
At the domain endpoint x=3,it has absolute minimum0.
problems.answer: No interior extrema; absolute minimum f(3)=0.
problems.note: The printed no-extrema choice uses the convention of excluding domain endpoints. If endpoints count,3 is a minimum and is not supplied alone among the choices.

problems.question: Find the decreasing interval of x³−x²−x+199.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The derivative is negative between its roots−1/3 and1.

problems.title: An inflection point
problems.question: Find inflection points of x⁵+5x³.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The positive factor2x²+3 means f″ changes sign only at x=0.
The graph point is(0,0).

problems.title: An integral of a logarithmic derivative
problems.question: Evaluate∫(2x+3)/(x²+3x+7)dx.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The numerator is the derivative of the denominator,which is always positive since its discriminant is9−28<0.
steps: Use u=x²+3x+7,du=(2x+3)dx.

problems.title: Area between a line and parabola
problems.question: Find area bounded by y=x² and y=x+2.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The line is above the parabola between them.
Area=∫₋₁²(x+2−x²)dx=[x²/2+2x−x³/3]₋₁²=9/2.

problems.title: Rotate a triangle about a non-symmetry bisector
problems.question: In isosceles ABC,AB=3,BC=AC=6. Rotate the triangle about the B-angle bisector. Find the solid volume.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: Along the bisector axis,take B=0,A=(3c,3s),C=(6c,−6s). Side AC crosses the axis at D=(4c,0).
The swept solid is the cone from B to the circle traced by C,minus the cone from D to that same circle. Their heights are6c and2c,and radius6s.
Volume=(π/3)(6s)²(6c−2c)=48πs²c.

problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.

problems.title: Surface-area ratio of two cone spheres
problems.question: A cone has slant height equal to base diameter. Find circumsphere-area divided by insphere-area.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Let base radius r,slant2r,height√3r. Insphere radiusρ=rh/(r+2r)=r/√3.
steps: Circumsphere radius R=(h²+r²)/(2h)=2r/√3.
Surface areas scale as squared radii,so the ratio is(R/ρ)²=4.

problems.title: Cone lateral area from a 30-degree generator angle
problems.question: Two cone generators make30°. Their endpoint chord is a side of an inscribed square. The base circumference is18π cm. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: Lateral area=πrl=81π(√3+1).

problems.title: A largest quadrilateral pyramid in a cylinder
problems.question: Find the largest volume of a quadrilateral pyramid with vertices on a cylinder of radius2,height6.
problems.idea: The listed answer16 applies to a pyramid based in a circular end face;the printed unrestricted wording allows larger examples.
formulas: Volume=base area times perpendicular apex distance divided by3.
steps: A square in a circular end base has area8;an apex in the other end plane gives volume8·6/3=16.
However,take a vertical rectangular base with vertices(1,±√3,0),(1,±√3,6). Every vertex lies on the cylinder of radius2,height6.
This rectangle has area(2√3)·6=12√3. Choose apex(−2,0,3),also on the cylinder. Its perpendicular distance to the base plane x=1 is3.
The pyramid volume is(12√3)·3/3=12√3>18,exceeding every printed numerical option.
problems.answer: As printed,none of the listed choices can be the maximum. With the intended extra condition that the pyramid base lies in a cylinder end base,the answer is16.
problems.note: The base location is not specified. A valid vertical-base pyramid has volume12√3≈20.785,so the commonly intended16 is not the unrestricted maximum.
